tagline: Down the Potomac beside a canal that stopped at Cumberland.
intro: The canal was meant to reach the Ohio. The railroad won the race west, and work stopped at Cumberland in 1850, eight years after the trains had arrived there. From Cumberland the byway follows the Potomac down toward Washington, dipping into West Virginia near the Paw Paw Tunnel and coming back at Hancock, then on by Williamsport and Sharpsburg, the river on one hand and the towpath never far off.

The canal fell 605 feet through 74 locks on its 184.5 miles, and the boats carried mostly coal down out of the Alleghenies until a flood shut it for good in 1924. Walked or biked from west to east, the towpath runs downhill.

moments.title: Paw Paw Tunnel
moments.text: Six million bricks line 3,118 feet of tunnel cut to skip six miles of river bends. Promised in two years, it took fourteen and nearly broke the canal company.

moments.title: Williamsport
moments.text: At Cushwa Basin the Conococheague Aqueduct, Lockhouse 44 and the canal's only railroad lift bridge stand within half a mile, and a canal launch still takes passengers out.

moments.title: Great Falls
moments.text: The rapids that closed the river to boats and gave the canal its reason. From the old tavern a mule-drawn barge still works through a lift lock.
